title: CIM-MLC: A Multi-level Compilation Stack for Computing-In-Memory Accelerators
problem: Existing open-source compilation stacks like TVM lack architectural support for diverse CIM accelerators, forcing CIM designs to either manually deploy networks or build custom compilers. Current compilation approaches are bound to fixed CIM architectures and cannot support architectures with different computing granularity (device precision, crossbar size, crossbar count).
motivation: Computing-in-memory processors demonstrate superior performance over traditional architectures, but unleashing their potential requires flexible compilation tools that are aware of diverse CIM architectural details and implementation diversity.
method: CIM-MLC introduces a multi-level compilation stack that abstracts CIM architectural diversity through multiple compilation layers. The stack supports variable device precision, crossbar configurations, and computing granularity without binding to fixed architectures. It extends beyond limited crossbar-bound operations to handle diverse operation types through flexible abstraction at each compilation level.
key_novelty: A multi-level compilation abstraction that flexibly supports diverse CIM architectures with different computing granularity and operation types without architectural lock-in.
contributions: Multi-level compilation stack architecture for diverse CIM accelerators
Support for varying device precision, crossbar sizes, and crossbar counts
Flexible handling of diverse operation scheduling beyond matrix-vector multiplication
Framework enabling CIM deployment without custom compiler development
